title: They Condemned It Before They Read It
paragraphs:
They Condemned It Before They Read It
What Jesus Exposed About Tradition, Judgment, and the Hearts That Refuse to Listen
Some people have already decided they disagree before they even know what was said.
They see a title.
They hear a rumor.
They notice a word that challenges what they have always believed.
And before a single sentence is read, before a single Scripture is examined, before a single prayer is whispered, the verdict has already been announced.
Guilty.
Wrong.
Dangerous.
Heretical.
Rejected.
What is astonishing is that this is not merely a modern problem.
It is an ancient one.
In fact, the same spirit that causes people to judge an article before reading it is the very spirit Jesus confronted throughout His earthly ministry.
Many imagine that if they had lived during the days of Christ, they would have immediately recognized Him.
Yet Scripture reveals something far more uncomfortable.
The people who rejected Jesus most aggressively were often the people most confident in their religious traditions.
They knew the customs.
They knew the ceremonies.
They knew the debates.
They knew the opinions of respected teachers.
Yet many never truly listened to the One standing before them.
The tragedy is captured in the words of Jesus Himself:
"Why do you also transgress the commandment of God because of your tradition?" (Matthew 15:3)
The Greek word translated "tradition" is παράδοσις (paradosis), meaning teachings handed down from previous generations.
Traditions themselves are not automatically evil. Some traditions can preserve truth and wisdom.
The danger begins when tradition becomes more authoritative than God's Word.
The danger begins when inherited beliefs become untouchable.
The danger begins when people defend what they have always heard rather than honestly examining what God has actually said.
Jesus repeatedly exposed this danger.
In Mark 7:13 He rebuked religious leaders for:
"Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition."
The Greek phrase "ἀκυροῦντες τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ" (akyrountes ton logon tou Theou) literally means "nullifying" or "canceling" God's Word.
Think about that.
People can become so committed to defending their traditions that they end up fighting against the very truth they claim to protect.
That should terrify every believer.
Because none of us are immune.
Not pastors.
Not teachers.
Not scholars.
Not ministry leaders.
Not authors.
Not readers.
Not you.
Not me.
Every one of us carries assumptions.
Every one of us possesses theological blind spots.
Every one of us has inherited beliefs that deserve honest examination under the light of Scripture.
The Bereans understood this.
Acts 17:11 praises them because they did not blindly accept what they heard.
Nor did they blindly reject it.
Instead:
"They received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so."
Notice the balance.
They listened first.
Then they investigated.
They were open enough to hear.
Yet careful enough to verify.
Many people today reverse that process.
They reject first.
Then refuse to investigate.
And in doing so they may miss truths God desires to show them.
The irony is heartbreaking.
The same people who criticize others for being closed-minded often become closed-minded themselves whenever their own traditions are challenged.
This is not merely an intellectual issue.
It is a heart issue.
Jesus consistently taught that truth encounters the condition of the heart before it encounters the condition of the mind.
The Hebrew word often used for heart is לֵב (lev).
In biblical thought, the heart was not merely the center of emotions.
It represented the deepest core of a person's will, desires, motives, understanding, and decisions.
That means spiritual blindness is not always caused by lack of information.
Sometimes it is caused by resistance.
Sometimes people do not reject truth because they cannot understand it.
Sometimes they reject truth because accepting it would require change.
And change is expensive.
Change threatens comfort.
Change challenges identity.
Change forces humility.
Change demands surrender.
That is why Jesus was so controversial.
He did not simply challenge false doctrines.
He challenged human pride.
The Aramaic name Jesus likely heard throughout His earthly life was יֵשׁוּעַ (Yeshua).
His very name means "The Lord saves."
Yet many who longed for a Messiah rejected the Savior standing directly in front of them because He did not fit their expectations.
Imagine missing the Messiah because He did not align with your tradition.
Imagine rejecting truth because it arrived in a package you did not expect.
Imagine standing before the Author of life while insisting your inherited assumptions were more trustworthy than His voice.
Yet that is exactly what happened.
And if we are not careful, it can happen to us.
This article is not asking readers to abandon biblical truth.
Quite the opposite.
It is a plea to return to biblical truth.
To test every claim by Scripture.
To compare every teaching with God's Word.
To refuse blind acceptance.
But also to refuse blind rejection.
Because truth never fears examination.
If something is false, Scripture will expose it.
If something is true, Scripture will confirm it.
The answer is not intellectual arrogance.
The answer is humble investigation.
The answer is prayerful study.
The answer is a heart willing to follow Jesus wherever His Word leads.
Even when it challenges us.
Even when it surprises us.
Even when it confronts traditions we have carried for years.
Perhaps that is why this message feels so personal.
Many readers know exactly what it feels like to be judged without being heard.
To be criticized by people who never actually listened.
To be dismissed before they finished reading.
To be misunderstood by those who already decided what they believed.
Jesus understands that pain.
He experienced it constantly.
People quoted Him out of context.
Misrepresented His words.
Spread false accusations.
Questioned His motives.
Rejected Him without truly hearing Him.
Yet He continued speaking truth.
He continued extending grace.
He continued inviting people to come and see.
And that invitation still stands today.
Before you reject a message, read it.
Before you condemn an idea, examine it.
Before you defend a tradition, test it.
Before you criticize, investigate.
Not because every new idea is correct.
But because every claim deserves to be measured by God's Word rather than human assumptions.
The Gospel has never been about protecting human traditions.
The Gospel is about redemption.
The Gospel is about grace.
The Gospel is about Jesus Christ transforming hearts.
The Gospel is about God taking broken stories and writing beautiful endings.
That is why our ministry exists.
Not to win arguments.
Not to create controversy.
Not to build personalities.
But to point people toward Jesus Christ.
Every article we publish is written with one prayer:
That someone who feels lost might find hope.
That someone trapped in shame might discover grace.
That someone buried beneath religion might encounter Christ.
That someone defending traditions might begin seeking truth.
And that someone who believes their story is over might discover that Jesus is still writing it.
If this article challenged you, encouraged you, or strengthened your faith, do not keep it to yourself.
Someone in your family may need this message.
Someone silently searching for truth may encounter Jesus because you chose to share.
Be honest.
Have you ever judged something before fully understanding it?
Have you ever defended a tradition before examining Scripture for yourself?
Let that be your prayer today.
Your support allows us to continue creating Christ-centered articles, biblical resources, discipleship materials, devotionals, teachings, and Gospel outreach that point people to Jesus.
If you truly desire to glorify God through your resources, partnering with ministries that faithfully proclaim Christ is one practical way to do so.
Because one article can change a perspective.
One perspective can change a heart.
One heart can change a family.
One family can change a generation.
And Jesus is still changing lives every day.
The people who condemned Him thought the story was ending.
They never realized grace was only beginning.
